answer: Coordinated-action deposit pricing. Each agent identity must anchor its actions to a shared coordination pool; the pool charges a rising deposit per additional identity that acts within the same short window. Multiple identities acting together thus pay a superlinear deposit, while a lone agent pays little. Deposits release at dawn after a verification epoch; duplicates forfeit them. An attacker's per-identity cost grows with the plume of synchronized accounts, making mass coordination expensive.
